layers.authority: Northern Land Council (Top End), for Traditional Owners
layers.process: A written permit is needed to enter Aboriginal land or waters in the NLC's area for any purpose, including using private roads. Traditional Owners can ask to see it.

layers.authority: Central Land Council, for Traditional Owners
layers.process: Traditional Owners' permission is needed to enter or remain on Aboriginal land in Central Australia; the CLC issues permits. Routes into WA land need a separate Ngaanyatjarra Council permit.

sources.title: Permits
sources.supports: Traditional Owners' permission; CLC issues permits

zone-requirements.note: Lead times are planning buffers (an older source says two to three weeks); ask each council.

own_names: Each estate has its own Traditional Owners and language names; the land councils name the group for your area when they consult.
culture-and-protocol.welcome_and_acknowledgement: Entry itself is by Traditional Owners' permission, given in writing through the Northern Land Council (Top End) or the Central Land Council (Central Australia). A verbal invitation still needs the written permit.
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: Stay inside your permitted area and keep to sacred site restrictions; on the Cox Peninsula the NLC says it is the visitor's responsibility to know where sacred sites are.
culture-and-protocol.photography_and_story_permissions: CLC: don't photograph people without their permission; private photos need no media permit, but commercial or published work needs a media permit. NLC: filming and recording need a work permit (media) and follow its media protocols.
culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Follow Traditional Owners' instructions; carry the permit and show it when asked. Alcohol is prohibited on Aboriginal land in the CLC area (transit visitors may carry it unopened); follow each community's alcohol rules.
culture-and-protocol.cultural_authority: Traditional Owners, through the Northern Land Council and the Central Land Council.
culture-and-protocol.source: Northern Land Council and Central Land Council permit pages

closures: Closures for funerals and ceremonies can happen at short notice; the NLC emails or texts permit holders in the affected area. The CLC says permits are refused mainly for ceremony, large funerals or rain-damaged roads.
protocol_notes: Keep your contact details current with the land council so closure notices reach you.

seasons-and-flow.notes: Two very different regions: the tropical Top End (NLC area) and arid Central Australia (CLC area), where the Wet/Dry split doesn't hold and summer heat is the main hazard. Visitor flow follows Tourism NT's Dry-season framing; no monthly counts were found. Check the NT road report before driving: unsealed roads close fast after rain.
